behavior_rows.claim: Every current skill has Codex metadata whose implicit-invocation policy agrees with the frozen Claude invocation class: user-invoked skills opt out of implicit invocation, while model-invoked skills do not carry that opt-out.
behavior_rows.adjudication: All 37 current skills have agents/openai.yaml metadata. The completed Phase 3 invocation join found 37/37 policies joined and zero Claude-to-Codex invocation mismatches. Frozen user-invoked examples explicitly set policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false; model-invoked examples omit that opt-out. The metadata is machine-readable, but this audit has not yet observed an actual Codex runtime loading and obeying every file.
behavior_rows.next_evidence: Runtime-observe representative user-invoked and model-invoked skills in Codex, then sample boundary cases if the harness behavior differs from the static contract.

behavior_rows.claim: The marketplace descriptor exposes one mattpocock-skills plugin sourced from the repository root and presents it as an installable Claude Code engineering-skills plugin.
behavior_rows.adjudication: The frozen marketplace.json contains a single plugin named mattpocock-skills with source './' and an engineering-skills description. This is machine-readable distribution metadata, but successful marketplace installation has not been runtime-observed in this audit.
behavior_rows.next_evidence: Exercise marketplace discovery/install against the frozen-compatible distribution path during Phase 7 runtime verification.

behavior_rows.claim: The HITL helper mechanically pauses for user actions and captures observations for the agent, while secret-sensitive guidance such as leaving sign-in to a non-captured step is advisory rather than technically enforced.
behavior_rows.adjudication: The shell functions step() and capture() mechanically block on terminal input and print captured values at the end. The file explicitly warns that capture echoes values back to the terminal and says signing in should remain a step, but nothing in the function prevents a caller from capturing a secret. The safety boundary therefore depends on correct template editing.
behavior_rows.next_evidence: Run the template with benign inputs and test whether a misuse-resistant guard is warranted; do not use real credentials.

behavior_rows.claim: At a phase boundary the documented decision tree checks Continue, /clear, /handoff, subagent, then /compact in that order, treating every non-Continue transition as a lossy conversion from primary to secondary context.
behavior_rows.adjudication: PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md explicitly defines the five options, states that the first yes wins, places /compact last as the default rather than first reach, and explains the primary-to-secondary information loss. These are judgement/prompt rules, not executable policy.
behavior_rows.next_evidence: Later compare real routing decisions against this ordered tree during red-team verification, especially ambiguous boundaries.

behavior_rows.claim: Engineering exploration should read relevant CONTEXT/CONTEXT-MAP and ADR material when present, proceed silently when absent, use glossary vocabulary, and surface ADR conflicts instead of silently overriding them.
behavior_rows.adjudication: domain.md gives explicit before-exploring reads, absence handling, glossary vocabulary rules, and ADR-conflict behavior. No executable checker enforces those obligations.
behavior_rows.next_evidence: Observe a setup/exploration run in repos with present, absent, and conflicting domain docs.

behavior_rows.claim: The local tracker stores specs and one-file-per-ticket issues under .scratch, uses explicit Status/Type/Blocked-by fields, and defines claim-before-work plus resolve-and-link-back semantics for wayfinding.
behavior_rows.adjudication: issue-tracker-local.md defines exact paths, numbering, state fields, frontier scan, claiming, resolution and map update behavior. The contract is procedural; no parser or lock is provided here to enforce atomic claims or valid state transitions.
behavior_rows.next_evidence: Runtime-test concurrent/duplicate claiming and malformed status files before treating the local tracker as robust coordination machinery.

behavior_rows.claim: Mocks are reserved for system boundaries; internal collaborators and owned modules should not be mocked, and external interfaces should be designed for narrow dependency injection.
behavior_rows.adjudication: mocking.md clearly separates system-boundary mocks from internal collaborators and gives dependency-injection/SDK-style guidance. There is no static test-lint rule in this surface that prevents internal mocking.
behavior_rows.next_evidence: Red-team the TDD workflow with codebases that already use internal mocks and see whether the operative skill follows or overrides this support rule.

behavior_rows.claim: Tests should verify observable behavior through public interfaces, avoid implementation-detail and tautological assertions, and survive internal refactors.
behavior_rows.adjudication: tests.md defines good integration-style behavior tests and concrete red flags for implementation-detail, external-bypass and tautological tests. These standards are guidance rather than a machine-enforced test-quality gate.
behavior_rows.next_evidence: Use adversarial examples during Phase 9 to test whether the operative TDD skill rejects brittle tests that still pass.

behavior_rows.claim: Rejected enhancements are persisted one file per concept under .out-of-scope, consulted by semantic concept similarity on future requests, and changed only with maintainer confirmation/reconsideration.
behavior_rows.adjudication: OUT-OF-SCOPE.md defines durable rejection records, semantic deduplication, maintainer confirm/reconsider/disagree branches, and the narrow write condition of rejected enhancement-as-wontfix. Matching and record maintenance are agent judgement, not executable enforcement.
behavior_rows.next_evidence: Test near-duplicate and superficially similar requests to measure false-positive/false-negative semantic matching during red-team verification.

behavior_rows.claim: Learning records are created lazily, numbered sequentially, capture demonstrated non-trivial understanding or prior knowledge rather than mere coverage, and preserve superseded understanding instead of deleting it.
behavior_rows.adjudication: LEARNING-RECORD-FORMAT.md defines lazy creation, sequential numbering, evidence-oriented write conditions, non-qualifying cases, and supersession. No schema validator or numbering lock is supplied by this file.
behavior_rows.next_evidence: Observe Teach across repeated sessions, including a corrected misconception and concurrent/new record numbering edge case.

behavior_rows.claim: A teaching workspace has one concise, concrete mission whose why, observable success criteria, constraints and out-of-scope boundaries steer subsequent teaching and are revised when reality changes.
behavior_rows.adjudication: MISSION-FORMAT.md defines the workspace-root artifact, template and rules including one mission per workspace, concrete outcomes, pushback on vagueness, revision on goal shift and brevity. These are prompt-level constraints.
behavior_rows.next_evidence: Runtime-observe mission creation and a mid-course mission change to verify downstream teaching actually reorients.

behavior_rows.claim: Explainer knowledge should come from curated high-trust resources, wisdom from listed communities, every resource should be annotated, gaps made explicit, weak sources pruned, and community opt-outs remembered.
behavior_rows.adjudication: RESOURCES-FORMAT.md explicitly says knowledge should be drawn from the curated file rather than parametric guesses, separates Knowledge and Wisdom, requires annotations, gaps and pruning, and records community preferences. Source quality and community usefulness still depend on external evidence and agent judgement.
behavior_rows.next_evidence: Test Teach on a topic with incomplete resources to verify it surfaces gaps rather than filling them from unsupported model guesses.
